claims.quote: Next round's adversary card is face up all round, and the agents waiting to land are in open view. (The threat, Unity and Discord decks stay hidden.)
claims.engine: The next event card is revealed a round ahead; Peek is the only look-ahead op and shows only adversary event cards.

claims.quote: Each country has a military base for each of its fronts, on an open hex by that border (the layout for your player count shows where).
claims.engine: place_bases puts each base on an open hex of the country touching the other country, chosen per layout.

claims.quote: Hardening token: saves one facility or node once (§13)
claims.engine: A hardening token on the hex is one Guard option for any piece destroyed there, removed when spent.

claims.quote: Firewall: no agent lands on its hex (§16)
claims.engine: place() and moves refuse agent arrivals on a firewalled hex; troops are not affected.

claims.quote: One standard action is the exception: Take down a botnet needs only your ambassador on the botnet, §8.
claims.engine: botnet_targets checks only for the seat's ambassador on a botnet hex, with no reach test; every other map-targeting standard action checks reach.

claims.quote: Lay out the map for the number of players, as its layout shows: one country each, and a military base on each base hex.
claims.engine: Map::build uses the layout for the country count and places bases on it.

claims.quote: build the event deck: deal the number of stage I, II and III cards your level asks for (§21; level 0: 4, 4 and 3) ... Turn the top card face up
claims.engine: stage_cards [4,4,3]; setup shuffles each stage, deals that many, stacks them and reveals the top card.

claims.quote: put one round's agent income into each country's pool beside the map (1 a country at level 0); shuffle the project deck and fill the adversary board's project slots (§17).
claims.engine: Setup fills the pools with ambassador_income[0]=0 plus Garrisons +1, then shuffles the project deck and deals the slots.

claims.quote: Then play round 1 (§4). Its round start and Sway step come first, as in every round, so the adversary's turn comes before anyone acts.
claims.engine: Round order opens with alignment.sway and then adversary.event; round_start hooks run before phase 0.

claims.quote: B: The event card acts (threats, agents, troops, corruption), troops march, the next card turns up, agents and compute come in.
claims.engine: Order: event, threats.deal, build, corrupt, natural, march, reveal (plus pool fill), compute.

claims.quote: E Production: Everything pays (the income step), then cities grow factories.
claims.engine: Growth first adds the extra drones (Warmongering, Arms Race, Conscription) and only then grows factories.
claims.fix: Everything pays (the income step), then growth: extra drones, and cities grow factories.

claims.quote: After every action and every step, check the tracks: put any Unity just gained on its track or against Discord, then tip any full track, Discord first (§12). Then check the ways to lose, then the purge (§14). If you would win and lose at once, you lose.
claims.engine: alignment.after places Unity, tips Discord then Unity in a loop, checks loss, then the purge.

claims.quote: Wall (Protector): adversary troops can't move onto, land on or strike a hex with your node (a troop that would land there stays in the supply). Only troops are stopped
claims.engine: walled() blocks step_toward, land_troops (troop stays in supply), moves.may_arrive and troop_targets_on.

claims.quote: (Production isn't a landing: an adversary factory on that hex still makes its troop there, which marches off.)
claims.engine: factory_output places a troop on the adversary factory with no Wall check; troop_steps_from lets a troop on a walled hex walk off.

claims.quote: The Militarist answers it: each turn, 1 troop lands in each country where you have a node (§6, its board).
claims.engine: wall_pressure lands the troop only on the country's lowest-numbered adversary or neutral factory. With no such factory nothing lands, and if your node stands on that factory the troop stays in the supply. From level 2 it lands 2.
claims.fix: The Militarist answers it: each turn, in each country where you have a node, a troop lands on its lowest-numbered adversary or neutral factory, if it has one (§6, its board).

claims.quote: Vigil: when an adversary troop ends its march next to one of your nodes, gain 1 insight. It pays once per troop per march; a troop that strikes doesn't count.
claims.engine: march_troops calls on_march_end once for each live troop whose end hex is next to the seat's node; a troop that strikes is spent (alive=false) and never pays.

claims.quote: It pays in any march: the adversary's turn's (spend it this round) or one a card or threat starts at once (a threat's comes after the action phase, so its insight is lost).
claims.engine: Only one op starts an immediate march: MarchNow, which needs a threat context and appears on one threat ('3 adversary Troops land here and march at once'). No card starts a march.
claims.fix: It pays in any march: the adversary's turn's (spend it this round) or the one a threat starts at once (that comes after the action phase, so its insight is lost).

claims.quote: Example. The Builder has placed 3 economy nodes (the setup node included) and none from the card-play track ... fourth space costs 1 more: 2 energy
claims.engine: Setup sets track_key to 1 for the setup node; economy_track[3].cost=1 and play_track[0] has no cost.

claims.quote: The other six, printed on your board, are conversions, draws and sacrifice powers, paid by discarding a card with a tag (§7, Tags).
claims.engine: The rule moved to §7 unchanged.

claims.quote: Troops where the Protector stands: in each country where the Protector has a node, Muster 1 on its lowest-numbered adversary or neutral factory, never a player's; with none, none lands (step 6).
claims.engine: wall_pressure filters to factory hexes with no player cube and lands deterministically on the lowest-numbered one.

claims.quote: each gets the pool divided by the number of sites, rounded down ... A country with no site of type X lands nothing: its pool goes back to the supply.
claims.engine: rally_plan gives n/k to each site; rally zeroes the pool before planning, and with no site it tallies rally_nowhere and places nothing.

claims.quote: Troops where the Protector stands (the Militarist's board, above): Muster 1 in each country with the Protector's node.
claims.engine: Runs after the card's twists and before projects; the factory condition is given in the board rule above.

claims.quote: A troop landing does nothing to them until it marches (below).
claims.engine: place_troop only adds the token; ambassadors on the troop's hex are removed one per step in the march.

claims.quote: city 4, station 3, factory 3 (each 1 fewer from level 1, §21), open land 3, and a hex with a node 2
claims.engine: corrupt_cut [1,1,1,0] from level 1 in the order City, Station, Factory, Land; a node takes no cut.

claims.quote: a city with your node loses the node at 2 agents, and corrupts only at its own number
claims.engine: Natural corruption checks cities at their number, then Node targets (any hex with a node) at 2.

claims.quote: A corruption marker on a city counts as an agent there, for corruption only.
claims.engine: Markers are counted only in the corruption held() count; claim_cost and city_dark read agents only.

claims.quote: Its targets are the places of that type the adversary doesn't own. Every agent next to a target moves onto it (... agents already on a target stay)
claims.engine: converge marks targets with corrupt_target and moves agents from non-target hexes next to an open target.

claims.quote: A site (city, station, factory): the adversary's cube replaces any owner's cube. Any node on that hex is destroyed (unless something protects it, §13), then every ambassador on it is removed. No corruption marker.
claims.engine: corrupt_hex runs take_for_adversary, destroy_piece on the node, removes ambassadors, then clear_markers_on, which also takes off the node's marker.

claims.quote: Open land: the same, and the hex gets a land corruption token
claims.engine: For Land, corrupt_hex adds a land-corruption token in place of take_for_adversary, so no adversary cube goes on. A node there is still destroyed and ambassadors removed.
claims.fix: Open land: no cube goes on, but any node there is destroyed and ambassadors removed as for a site, and the hex gets a land corruption token: ...

claims.quote: A node hex (2 agents): only the node is lost (§13 applies), and like any lost node it leaves a corruption marker.
claims.engine: lose_node leaves a marker only if the hex holds no marker, botnet or adversary cube. A node on a corrupted site or a botnet hex (a liberated station keeps its botnet) leaves none, as §13 itself says.
claims.fix: A node hex (2 agents): only the node is lost (§13 applies), leaving a corruption marker as any lost node does (§13: not where a marker, botnet or adversary cube already is).

claims.quote: if an ambassador (any player's) stands on the troop's hex, the troop removes one (the players choose whose): that is its step, and the troop stays, so it can remove two in a turn
claims.engine: A step that starts on a hex with an ambassador removes one and continues to the next step without moving.

claims.quote: and a troop mustered onto your factory strikes it in the same turn's march (an ambassador standing there takes one of its steps first).
claims.engine: Each ambassador on the troop's hex takes a whole step. With 2 ambassadors there (or 2 steps used otherwise) the troop never strikes that turn, and the players may pick another target on or next to it.
claims.fix: and a troop mustered onto your factory strikes it (or another target in range) in the same turn's march, unless ambassadors standing there use up its steps first (one each).

claims.quote: Build a hand. Each player takes the top card of the tier-1 or the tier-2 deck, your choice each time, one at a time until they have 4.
claims.engine: Action::Tier deals the top card of the chosen tier, card by card, up to deal=4.

claims.quote: Solo, you take all 4, then keep those you want, paying as below.
claims.engine: With one seat the packet passes back to itself, and the keep phase prices each keep as usual.

claims.quote: They do count for its own per-tag gains, which print "(including this)", except on an event.
claims.engine: Reworded from the old sentence; no change in meaning.

claims.quote: Sacrifice. A cost that names a tag ("1 Industry") is paid by discarding one of your cards in play that carries that tag ...
claims.engine: sacrifice_for pays power and threat tag costs alike from cards in play.

claims.quote: An Effect fires once for each action that sets it off ..., however many pieces that action removed or tokens it placed, with no limit a round (§23).
claims.engine: Reworded from the old sentence; no change in meaning.

claims.quote: Claim: ambassadors: city 5, station or factory 3, +1 an agent; Liberate: ambassadors, as Claim
claims.engine: claim_city 5, claim_station 3, claim_factory 3, liberate_at 5, liberate_facility_at 3, each +1 per agent.

claims.quote: Take down a botnet: remove a botnet from a hex where your ambassador stands, in reach or not (the ambassador stays)
claims.engine: There is no reach check, and the ambassador stays.

claims.quote: Buy energy: ... each city once a round, for all players together
claims.engine: bought_key is per city, not per seat.

claims.quote: So an agent and an ambassador never share a hex.
claims.engine: Every way an agent or ambassador arrives (place, converge, moves.arrive, place_ambassador) cancels one for one before adding a token.

claims.quote: Remove agents removes its agents one at a time, your choice, and you may stop early.
claims.engine: The first removal is mandatory; after that each one is offered with a stop option.

claims.quote: (Agents and your ambassadors never share a hex, so a site with agents is paid from your supply.)
claims.engine: pay_site spends the seat's own ambassadors on the site first, and there are none where agents stand.

claims.quote: Liberate cards ... liberate a corrupted city in reach as Liberate does, for the card's own price instead of ambassadors.
claims.engine: liberate_city calls liberate_site unpaid on a liberable city in reach.

claims.quote: A megaproject holding 8 cubes or more completes, once: every cube on it pays, overflow included (§8), then its cubes come off ... From then on its stations' cubes go to their owners' boards (step 3).
claims.engine: complete_projects zeroes the cubes, sets project_done and pays each cube; station_cubes then sends cubes to the boards.

claims.quote: Every round, every city builds one factory on a free industrial zone (one with no factory, station or land corruption; a node doesn't count) ... a blocked city builds too. A destroyed factory leaves the map and frees its zone.
claims.engine: free_zones checks only industrial, no building and no land corruption; grow_factories has no blocking check; destroy_piece removes the FACTORY token.

claims.quote: Tags: one player alone sacrifices cards in play carrying 2 matching tags in all (tier 1) or 3 (tier 2)
claims.engine: Every tier-1 sacrifice counter has amount 2 and every tier-2 one has amount 3.

claims.quote: Each base holds up to 2 drones; a base that is full takes no more.
claims.engine: Warmongering, Arms Race and Conscription add a drone past the cap (past_cap=true). §11 lists Warmongering as a source without that exception.
claims.fix: Each base holds up to 2 drones; a full base takes no more, except from Warmongering and some projects (§19).

claims.quote: every neutral factory puts 1 drone on each base of its own country (so 2 drones at 3-4 countries), unless an agent stands on it. Each ambassador on that factory stops one of its drones
claims.engine: tip_corp_troops: one drone per base of the country; in the 3- and 4-country layouts each country has 2 fronts; each player ambassador removes one.

claims.quote: An ambassador on a base stops each drone that would land there, from any source, one ambassador a drone, and is spent. A drone already at a base stays until war or a protection uses it up.
claims.engine: Every drone addition goes through corp_troops_at, which spends a base ambassador first; drones leave only in war (troops.rs:43) or as a Guard (destroy.rs:100).

claims.quote: Discord still tips, but to 0 instead of 2.
claims.engine: With carry=2 a tip subtracts the capacity: 9-9=0, against 11-9=2.

claims.quote: A track still full after a tip (what stayed, or a card that fills it) tips again at once.
claims.engine: The after() loop rechecks both tracks after every tip (up to 64 times).

claims.quote: Shelter ... It stops only what goes through this order: cubes still change hands, ambassadors are still removed, and a node you give up to pay something is still lost.
claims.engine: Shelter is checked only in destroy_piece. corrupt_hex still moves cubes and removes ambassadors, and pay-or-lose-node and counters call lose_node directly.

claims.quote: One hardening token on a hex with both your facility and your node can save either, once: you may keep it for the second. In war, saving the factory saves its node too (§11).
claims.engine: Harden is a guard for any piece on the hex, and the owner may decline it. The token stays while a node or facility remains. War destroys the node only after the factory is destroyed.

claims.quote: Round 12 (10 at levels 3-4) still opens with its Sway step, so a Discord tip can lose the game there first; then, with no card left, you lose.
claims.engine: 11 (or 9) cards are dealt, one revealed at setup; the round order puts alignment.sway before adversary.event, whose flip ends the game when the face-up pile is empty.

claims.quote: "open land": an open hex with no base, station, factory or land corruption, a node on it or not
claims.engine: corrupt_target(Land) requires HexKind::Open (bases are HexKind::Base), no building and no land corruption, with no node test.

claims.quote: Every agent next to a target moves onto it, across borders too, even off one of the adversary's own sites.
claims.engine: converge moves agents from any non-target hex, its neighbors in any country, adversary-owned hexes included.

claims.quote: A corruption marker on a city counts as an agent there (for corruption only: not for a Claim price or blocking).
claims.engine: claim_cost and city_dark count agents only.

claims.quote: each goes onto the cheapest project showing, by printed cost, however full (tie: the first slot)
claims.engine: pour_waiting takes min_by_key(project_cost) over the row in slot order.

claims.quote: A threat's two tokens never share a hex: place them in printed order, but if that would leave one off the map, place the type with fewer places first.
claims.engine: place_tokens tries printed order, and if a token goes unplaced, re-sorts by fewest sites.

claims.quote: A player's ambassador on a base stops the drone that base would get, whatever makes it ... With several players' ambassadors on one place, the earliest in player order is spent first.
claims.engine: corp_troops_at, used for every drone, spends player_ambassador(), which is the lowest seat.

claims.quote: Shelter (1 Security, 1 energy: in any one country, no node or facility can be destroyed from now to cleanup, §13)
claims.engine: The Shelter flag is checked in destroy_piece and cleared at cleanup.

claims.quote: Open Science: each round in the income step, give 2 insight ...
claims.engine: Paid in economy.upkeep, which ends the income step (wording only).

claims.quote: Each row is the whole level. Your own costs (claim, liberate, cards, actions) never change.
claims.engine: No difficulty parameter touches claim, liberate, card or standard-action prices; difficulty changes only adversary numbers and threat items.

claims.quote: Threat items: credits +4, other resources +1 (level 1); credits +4, other resources +2 (level 2+); a tag item never changes.
claims.engine: counter_bonus_all 1 and counter_bonus_credits 4 from level 1; counter_more_all 1 from level 2.

claims.quote: Muster: every Muster (an event card's, a project's, the Protector landing) lands 1 more troop in each country it lands in.
claims.engine: deploy_bonus (+1 from board_difficulty_at 2) is added per region in team::troops and in wall_pressure.

claims.quote: Each unpaid threat: a threat that takes effect unpaid also gives the adversary 4 compute, at its next compute step (§17). A threat that only waits gives none.
claims.engine: threat_compute (4 from level 2) is banked by gain_compute after each executed threat; a waiting threat continues before that line.

claims.quote: Solo: ... You take all 4 cards in the draft and keep those you want, paying as usual (§7).
claims.engine: Same as §7.

claims.quote: Brown box with a track arrow: raise your income of that resource for the rest of the game (arrow down would lower it; no card prints one yet)
claims.engine: track_move renders raise or lower; no card has 'lowers' or a negative production op.

claims.quote: Sway (a marker on a track): add Unity to the Unity track
claims.engine: The face draws Op::Sway with the same 'sway' icon for either side. The Nuclear Option prints sway side discord (1 Discord) with that icon, and Unity a card adds may also go against Discord (§12).
claims.fix: Sway (a marker on a track): add that much to a track: Unity (§12; you may put it against Discord), or Discord on the one card that says so (The Nuclear Option)

claims.quote: Peek (a card with an eye): look at the next event cards under the face-up one
claims.engine: Op::Peek shows the next N adversary deck cards beyond the face-up one.

claims.quote: Bricks: ... (not the Protector's Wall, which stops troops)
claims.engine: Firewalls and cordons stop agents; Wall stops troops.

claims.quote: Discord: the adversary's track; 6 Discord cards, and a 7th tip loses, §12.
claims.engine: alignment.json has 6 discord cards, discord_removed is 0, and a tip with an empty deck loses.

claims.quote: Rally X: an event line: each country's pool lands evenly on its sites of type X, §6.
claims.engine: As rally_plan.

claims.quote: Target: a place a Corrupt line can corrupt, §15; an adversary troop's targets are player facilities, §6.
claims.engine: Nodes become troop targets only at stage >= troop_node 4, which never happens (stages are 1-3).
